title: Navigating my Longer PCOS Cycles With Inito
summary: After a PCOS diagnosis and experiencing longer irregular cycles, Amanda Culp shares how tracking hormones with Inito helped her confirm ovulation and conceive with confidence.
body_markdown:
Story shared by Amanda Culp to Inito: This story reflects an individual’s experience.


Disclaimer: The success stories shared here represent individual experiences and outcomes. PCOS presents differently in each person, and results may vary based on medical history, lifestyle, and adherence to recommendations. This content is for educational purposes only and does not replace personalized medical advice. Please consult your healthcare provider before making health-related changes.


While I was also taking additional measures to address the PCOS, such as losing weight, working with a dietician, etc., I truly believe that we were able to conceive because of Inito’s data accuracy.


## How I Started TTC With PCOS and Longer Cycles


I was diagnosed with PCOS about three to four months before my husband and I were married in April 2024. I’ve never used hormonal birth control or[IUDs](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557403/) (An intrauterine device, is a small device that your doctor inserts into your uterus to prevent pregnancy) and have always preferred to avoid disrupting my hormones, so receiving that diagnosis pushed me to better understand what was happening in my body.


One of the biggest changes I noticed was in my cycle length. My cycles went from being fairly regular around 27-28 days to stretching out to 35-40 days. That shift became one of my main concerns, especially as we started thinking about trying to conceive.


## What Changed After My PCOS Diagnosis


As I began learning more about PCOS, I became increasingly aware of how different my cycles looked. The[longer cycle](https://blog.inito.com/why-is-my-menstrual-cycle-getting-longer/) length stood out, and not knowing when ovulation might actually be happening made the process feel uncertain.


Even before we were actively trying to conceive, that lack of clarity added stress. I wanted a better way to understand my cycle rather than relying on averages that no longer seemed to apply to my body.


## Why Longer Cycles Made Ovulation Hard to Predict


With my cycles stretching out to 35-40 days, it became harder to identify when my fertile window actually was. Not having solid confirmation around ovulation made timing stressful, especially once we started thinking seriously about trying to conceive.


I knew that if we were going to start TTC, I needed a way to better understand what my hormones were doing throughout those longer cycles.


## How I Found A Better Way to Track My Cycle


I first discovered Inito through an ad while clicking through stories. As I researched fertility monitors and compared different options, I found that Inito stood out for a few reasons.


It was significantly more affordable than many of the other monitors I was considering, had a much shorter wait time for results, and only required one stick to test four different hormones. I also came across more positive reviews from people with PCOS, which mattered to me given my longer cycles.


After weighing my options, those factors solidified my decision to try Inito.


## What Made Inito Different for Me


We purchased Inito in January 2024. We got married in April 2024, and around August 2024 is when we truly started trying to conceive. Until that point, we hadn’t been actively trying to achieve pregnancy, but the uncertainty around my longer cycles was still stressful.


Using Inito allowed us to get a clearer picture of where my fertile window actually fell within those longer cycles. Being able to see my hormone data and confirm ovulation gave us a much greater sense of peace of mind.


At the same time, I was also taking other steps to support my PCOS, including losing weight and working with a dietician. While there were multiple factors involved, I truly believe that Inito’s data accuracy played an important role in helping us conceive in September.


**


**


## Finding Support Beyond the Data


Once we confirmed our pregnancy and logged it in the Inito app, it suggested joining the Inito Moms-to-Be & Mamas support group.


What I appreciated most about the group was the range of experiences shared. Women posted about different stages of pregnancy, pregnancy loss, understanding hormone changes, celebrating babies being born, and asking questions about symptoms or concerns along the way.


While there were sometimes differing opinions especially around PCOS topics like progesterone supplementation, I appreciated hearing multiple perspectives and took what felt relevant to my own situation.


That mix of education, shared experience, and support made the community a meaningful part of my journey.


**


**
